messages:
rachel: heads-up: spike in GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1 starting ~01:05 UTC. pods show Pending then quickly Evicted.

omar: saw that. scheduler logs show assign -> immediate reclaim by kubelet. sample: 

omar: ```
scheduler: INFO assign pod job-42 -> ap-southeast1-node-07
kubelet: ERROR device-plugin lease failed: rpc timeout
kubelet: INFO reclaimed GPU 0 for pod job-42
```

sue: sounds like a timing window where scheduler thinks device is free but kubelet has transiently re-claimed it. could be device-plugin flapping or control-plane latency.

felix: node metrics show CPU and network OK, but device-plugin restarted on a few nodes around the spike. suspect plugin crash-looping after recent rollout.

rachel: rolling back device-plugin to previous build (v1.8.2) on affected nodes now. will also cordon nodes that reported plugin restarts >2 in 5m.

infra-bot: autoscaler: ap-southeast1 warm-pool 6 nodes, free 1. No scale events recorded in last 30m.

omar: temporary mitigation: add a short 3s scheduler allocation-hold before rescheduling a pod when we see a recent lease error. low-risk and reversible.

sue: agree. also add a metric to count 'double-claim' events for correlation.

felix: rollback complete for device-plugin on 8 nodes. eviction rate dropping.

rachel: cordoned noisy nodes and annotated them infra/device-noise=true. will uncordon after 15m stable.

infra-bot: alert cleared: gpu-eviction-rate normalised.

omar: follow-ups: INFRA-TKT-812 add scheduler hold, DEVOPS-299 improve device-plugin rollout healthchecks, DESCHED-201 simulate fragmentation impact from cordoning.

rachel: closing — root cause: device-plugin instability + tight scheduler reschedule window. :white_check_mark:
